job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, tonight I sat on the terrace observing the night sky with my telescope. It is fascinating to realize that the Sun is actually a star, just like the tiny points of light we see at night, but it appears larger because it is much closer to us. I spent time locating the Pole Star, which is famous not for being the brightest, but because it remains fixed in the northern sky while other stars appear to shift due to Earth's rotation. I also observed Jupiter, which shone steadily without twinkling, unlike the distant stars that flicker due to atmospheric disturbances. My little brother asked if the Moon changes shape because clouds cover it, but I explained that the phases are actually caused by the changing portion of the Moon's sunlit surface visible from Earth. We also saw a streak of light, which I told him was a meteor, or a 'shooting star,' caused by a small object burning up in our atmosphere, not a star falling from its place. It is amazing to think that our Earth is just one of many planets, and many of these planets have their own moons orbiting them, just as our Moon orbits us. The universe is truly vast and full of wonders that defy our simple daily observations.

items.evidence: It is fascinating to realize that the Sun is actually a star, just like the tiny points of light we see at night, but it appears larger because it is much closer to us.
items.q: Why does the Sun look so much larger than the stars we see at night?
options: Because it is much nearer to us
Because it is not a star at all
Because night stars are tiny, smaller than it
Because Earth's rotation makes it look large
items.explain: The Sun is a star like the others; it only looks larger because it is much closer.

wrong.why: thinks the Sun is not a star because it looks different
thinks stars really are smaller than the Sun
grabs Earth's rotation, a cause mentioned nearby

It moves east to west like the others
It grows brighter than every other star

items.explain: The Pole Star stays fixed in the northern sky while other stars seem to shift as Earth rotates.

wrong.why: thinks all stars really move across the sky

items.q: Meena sees a bright dot that does not flicker at all. What is it most likely?

A star, such as the Pole Star

A star very close to Earth

items.evidence: My little brother asked if the Moon changes shape because clouds cover it, but I explained that the phases are actually caused by the changing portion of the Moon's sunlit surface visible from Earth.
items.q: Why does the Moon seem to change shape over a month?
options: We see different amounts of its lit side
Clouds cover different parts of it
Earth's shadow falls across part of it
Its real size grows and then shrinks
items.explain: Phases happen because we see a changing part of the Moon's sunlit surface, not because of clouds.
